Hi Aditya,

Quick heads up from CartGrid Ops — between 2028-08-01 23:45 UTC and 2028-08-02 01:10 UTC we saw a sustained spike of 429s (rate-limit / throttling) from calls to the Redwood inference endpoint powering our checkout validation service. Impact: ~18% failed authorizations across a 1.4 hour window, several checkout sessions abandoned.

We pulled application-side traces and saw repeated 429 responses with X-Request-Id headers that map back to your endpoint. We're attaching a compressed trace bundle and our internal ticket (stubbed below) for your review. Can you confirm whether this meets the SLA "unavailable" or "degraded" definitions and advise on credit eligibility? We also need a post-incident timeline for our internal RCAs.

Attachments: [cartgrid_traces_20280802.tar.gz (log bundle)], [support_ticket_3421.pdf]

Thanks,
Amelia Park

Amelia / Aditya — I started an initial check of control-plane and serving logs for us-west-2. Quick findings: we see an elevated 429 rate from one of the fronting gateways during the window you reported.

Questions / asks for CartGrid to speed validation:
- Please confirm the tenant id or API key prefix used for the impacted calls (we need to map to request ownership).
- The trace bundle you shared contains client-side timeouts and repeated retries — can you confirm if your retry policy was aggressive (e.g., immediate retries) or if the clients backed off? That will affect our impact calculation.

We'll attempt to pull the server-side request traces tied to the X-Request-Id values in your bundle. Please confirm whether we have permission to pull additional telemetry from your tenant for the window above (we don't need any PII — just request/response headers and gateway logs).

Preliminary note: there was a short routing flap in the edge gateway pool that caused transient 429s while a buggy shard entered a degraded state; I'm not yet comfortable declaring SLA eligibility without computing request volumes and tenant weighting. We'll produce a time-series of error rate + request counts and propose an eligibility assessment.

Laura Bennett

Amelia — thank you for the permission and the trace bundle. Quick status update and next steps: 

What we did:
- Engineering extracted server-side request counts for TG-7884 and aligned them to your X-Request-Id markers.
- We computed per-tenant request volume and error-rate during the window (23:45–01:10 UTC).
- We identified a routing shard that returned 429s due to a degraded token bucket that failed to refill correctly after a transient memory pressure event.

Preliminary eligibility guidance:
- The incident meets our definition of a regional "degraded" window for the us-west-2 cluster; at the tenant level TG-7884 experienced an 18% failed authorization rate during the window.
- Final SLA credit eligibility requires a billing reconciliation and apportionment across multi-tenant impact. Marissa will pull billing lines and initiate the formal credit request.

Planned outcomes and timeline:
- Marissa (CS) will open a formal SLA claim on Monday, 2028-08-06, attaching the billing slice and your evidence.
- Engineering will prepare a post-incident report (RC A) with timeline, root cause, mitigations, and preventive actions within 7 business days (target by 2028-08-13).
- If CartGrid prefers an expedited credit calculation, reply to this thread and we will prioritize the finance reconciliation.

Action items for CartGrid:
- Confirm you want Redwood to proceed with a standard SLA claim (Marissa will need a signed SLA credits request form).
- Share any additional high-fidelity retry timing so we can better attribute duplicate vs. unique failed attempts.

I'll keep you posted and will schedule the postmortem invite once Marissa files the claim. Apologies again for the impact.

— Aditya Rao
